penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: GDPR/CCPA compliance tooling operates in a regulated legal context; erroneous audit trail generation or incomplete deletion workflows expose the operator and customers to legal liability.

rationale: The buyer is real and well-defined — Salesforce admins and compliance officers at SMB-to-mid-market B2C companies have budget authority, face regulatory deadlines, and demonstrably pay for compliance tooling (Salesforce AppExchange ISVs charge $15–$50/user/month for adjacent solutions). However, building this correctly requires deep Salesforce platform integration (Apex, Metadata API, field history retention configs), GDPR/CCPA legal accuracy guarantees, and per-org configuration work that a Claude prompt + simple page cannot deliver reliably — buildability and operational autonomy both sit at 5, failing their build_gate floors. The regulated_industry penalty (−1.5) drops the total to 4.8, below the validate threshold, because getting the deletion-plus-retention logic wrong is a compliance incident, not just a bad UX. This is the right problem but the wrong build for a solo non-technical operator without a Salesforce ISV program and legal review.
solution_plan: This micro-service would be a Salesforce-connected audit-trail generator: when a RTBF deletion fires, it auto-creates a pseudonymized record capturing what was deleted, when, who approved it, and any retained non-personal transaction data — all logged to an external store Claude can query later. Unfortunately, building this correctly is not feasible for a solo non-technical operator without a Salesforce developer partner: it requires Salesforce org-level API integration, Apex triggers or Flow configuration per customer, and legal sign-off on what 'pseudonymized' means under GDPR Article 17. The factory cannot ship a legally defensible compliance tool of this type using only Claude prompts and a simple page. If Youval has a Salesforce developer co-founder or a legal/compliance partner, revisit — the commercial opportunity is strong. Otherwise, drop.
notes: Failing build_gates: buildability_with_ai (5, floor is 6) and operational_autonomy (5, floor is 7). Even without the regulated_industry penalty, the total (5.8) with both gates failing would cap stage at validate. With the penalty the total falls to 4.8, below min_total_to_validate (5.5), yielding drop. Strong commercial signal — worth revisiting if technical complexity can be abstracted via a Salesforce ISV partner.
